title: Component-restriction finite-partition ring diagram
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative ring, $P=\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}C)$ with the quotient topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $S$ a topological space, and $f:S\to P$ continuous. For a subset $Z\subseteq P$ define $C_Z$ as the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of $C[1/e_W]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] over clopen subsets $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}C$ containing the inverse image of $Z$, with arrows for reverse inclusion; $e_W$ is the unique idempotent with $D(e_W)=W$. The transition maps are the canonical localization maps. Inclusion $Z\subseteq Z\prime$ induces the canonical restriction $C_{Z\prime}\to C_Z$. For a discrete quotient $Q$ of $S$ (an equivalence relation with open classes, with its quotient map $q_Q:S\to Q$), define $D_Q=\prod_{a\in Q}C_{f(q_Q^{-1}(a))}$ as a $C$-algebra. A refinement $Q\prime\leq Q$ gives $D_Q\to D_{Q\prime}$ by evaluating at the containing coarse class and applying the restriction map. Define the functor $Q\mapsto D_Q$ from the opposite of the refinement poset to $C$-algebras by these arrows. For profinite $S$, the quotients are exactly finite partitions into nonempty clopen subsets. The empty partition and its zero product ring are included. This defines the diagram for any continuous $f$; no w-locality, extremal disconnectedness or surjectivity is required.
